name: org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin
description: GW Maven Plugin is the Maven adapter for Machai Ghostwriter and its Guided File Processing workflow. It brings AI-assisted maintenance into Maven projects by scanning selected source code, tests, documentation, site content, configuration, and other project files. The gw:gw goal follows embedded @guidance instructions, while gw:act executes a reusable act or a direct prompt. Project-wide aggregator goals can coordinate multi-module traversal and Maven parallelism; gw-per-module and act-per-module let Maven schedule each reactor module. The plugin resolves Maven project, session, reactor, and settings context; accepts model, scan-path, instruction, exclusion, and provider configuration; reads credentials and custom values from Maven settings.xml server entries; and offers Java class discovery and reflection metadata to Ghostwriter. It is a Java 8-targeted Maven plugin for repeatable documentation automation, code review, content updates, and guided project maintenance.

usageContext: Source code, test, documentation, site, and configuration file processing
Project-wide and per-module Ghostwriter act execution
Java class discovery and reflective metadata inspection
integrations: GenAI model providers configured through Machai Ghostwriter

constructors.description: Declare the plugin in a Maven build, configure a Ghostwriter model and provider credentials, then invoke a guidance or act goal. Credentials can remain outside the project in Maven settings.xml.

examples.description: Step 1: add this plugin under build/plugins in pom.xml. Step 2: add a server whose id is my-ai-provider to Maven settings.xml. Step 3: run mvn gw:gw for embedded guidance or mvn gw:act with an act value.

features.name: gw
features.description: Runs project-wide guidance processing. Ghostwriter scans the selected path for embedded @guidance instructions and applies the requested changes using Maven project context. The aggregator goal can coordinate a multi-module project and receive Maven parallelism from -T.

examples.description: After installing or declaring the plugin, run this command at the Maven project root to process guidance in Markdown files, exclude generated output, review edits, and run normal verification.

features.name: act
features.description: Executes a predefined Ghostwriter act, an act followed by additional prompt text, or a direct prompt. A direct prompt begins with > so Ghostwriter does not interpret it as an act name. This aggregator goal can process a directory without a pom.xml.

examples.description: Step 1: configure the provider. Step 2: invoke the direct prompt from the project root. Step 3: retain the leading >, limit the scan to documentation, and review generated edits.

features.name: gw-per-module
features.description: Runs guidance processing for the current Maven reactor module. Use it when Maven should retain dependency-driven module ordering and each module must be processed within its own boundary.

examples.description: Configure the plugin in a multi-module parent or applicable modules, then run this command at the reactor root. Maven invokes the goal per module and Ghostwriter processes each selected source path.

features.name: act-per-module
features.description: Runs an act for each Maven reactor module. Use it when a reusable operation, such as documentation review, should be scoped and scheduled by Maven per module.

examples.description: Configure a reusable review act, invoke the command at the multi-module root, and let Maven schedule module execution while the plugin applies the act to each module path.

features.name: findClass
features.description: Finds fully qualified names whose simple class names match a regular expression in a registered Maven project's cached compile/test/output classpath. It returns at most 10 matches and is the discovery step before class inspection.

examples.description: Register an org.apache.maven.project.MavenProject through the constructor, search for implementation names ending in Mojo, then use one returned fully qualified name with getClassInfo.

features.name: getClassInfo
features.description: Returns reflective class metadata from a registered Maven project's class loader: inheritance, interfaces, annotations, non-private fields and methods, constructors, class location, dependency coordinates, and source path when available.

examples.description: Register the Maven project, supply an exact fully qualified class name and the same base directory, then use the resulting API and origin metadata to ground a documentation or analysis workflow.

customizations.name: gw.path
customizations.description: Selects a file, directory, glob, or supported scan pattern for guidance and act processing.

examples.description: Restricts guidance processing to project Markdown documentation.

customizations.name: genai.serverId
customizations.description: Selects the Maven settings.xml server entry used to obtain provider credentials and provider-specific configuration.

examples.description: Runs the review act using credentials and configuration held by the my-ai-provider Maven server entry.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run guidance-driven documentation maintenance
steps: Create a Maven settings.xml server entry containing the provider credentials and configure its id as serverId.
Place @guidance instructions in the documentation or source files that need repeatable maintenance.
Run mvn gw:gw -Dgw.path=src/site/markdown -Dgw.excludes=target,node_modules from the project root.
Review the edits, then run the normal Maven build and tests before committing both the instructions and resulting documentation.

examples.title: Run a one-time documentation prompt
steps: Configure the plugin and provider as in the guidance scenario.
Run mvn gw:act '-Dgw.act=>Update the project documentation' -Dgw.path=src/site/markdown from the project root.
Keep the leading > so the act argument is handled as direct user input rather than a predefined act name.
Inspect the modified files and validate them with the project's normal documentation and build checks.
